title: Develop drift-aware eval harness with cohort normalization
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: When we roll config changes (batching, quantization, kernel selection) or model variants, our global eval scores often move in ways that are driven by shifts in input distribution (query length, instruction style, task mix) rather than intrinsic quality regression. That produces noisy alerts, false positives for rollbacks, and under/over-reaction by engineering and SRE teams.

Goal: Build a drift-aware evaluation harness that produces cohort-normalized score deltas and calibrated uncertainty estimates for LLM-as-judge outputs. The harness should: 1) segment evals into meaningful cohorts, 2) compute normalized deltas per cohort using rolling baselines, 3) calibrate LLM-as-judge confidence (and rescale scores) with a lightweight online calibration model, and 4) emit actionable signals and gating decisions for config/model rollouts.

Scope: This ticket covers the product definition, acceptance criteria, and rollout plan for the new harness. Engineering tickets (ENG-21456, ENG-21901) will implement the runtime, storage, and dashboarding. Design work for visualizations will be tracked separately (DES-1120).
acceptance_criteria: Cohort definitions implemented: at minimum by intent (instruction vs. conversational), token length bins, and dataset-origin tags
Baseline window configured: rolling 30-day baseline with bootstrap CI computation
Normalization: system computes cohort-wise z-scores and a weighted aggregate drift index
LLM-as-judge calibration: produces reliability curves and outputs calibrated confidence in [0,1]
Alerting rules: drift index > threshold or calibrated mean delta < negative threshold triggers an alert with per-cohort breakdown
Gating integration: a pass/fail signal exported to rollout service for canary step evaluation
Dashboard: per-release view with cohort deltas, calibration plots, and historical drift trends
Docs: README + runbook describing interpretation, caveats, and follow-up steps for false positives
steps: Finalize cohort taxonomy with Research and Product (meetings week of 2025-02-17)
Specify statistical model for normalization (z-score vs. Bayesian hierarchical) and select default
Prototype small-scale calibration pipeline using held-out judge annotations and synthetic perturbations
Instrument eval harness to tag incoming evals with cohort metadata
Implement rolling baseline and CI computation (bootstrapped) in ENG backlog
Integrate calibrated LLM-as-judge outputs and compute adjusted deltas
Define alert thresholds and gating rules jointly with SRE and Rollouts team
Create dashboard mockups and iterate with Design
Run shadow-mode experiments for two weeks against 3 recent rollouts before flip to enforcement

2025-02-24: Chosen calibration strategy: isotonic regression for initial release due to monotonicity and low compute; Bayesian calibration considered for v2 (note in ENG-21901)
2025-03-03: Agreement to use 30-day rolling baseline with 7-day decay factor for recency weighting (Oliver)
2025-03-04: Decided alerts will include both statistical significance and minimum practical delta to avoid noise-driven notifications (SRE feedback)
review_feedback: Design review (2025-02-26): UX requested per-cohort drilldowns and inline examples of failing prompts (DES notes)
Eng design review (2025-02-28): ENG asked to add request-sampling to avoid compute spikes during large eval runs; agreed to cap sample rate at 10% for expensive judges
Research review (2025-03-01): Recommend adding adversarial perturbation set to surface brittleness and measure judge calibration under out-of-distribution examples
Security review (2025-03-03): No PII expected in eval payloads; confirm scrubbers are applied before storage (action assigned to ENG-21456)
